item.title: Saudi road authority uses vehicle simulator to test road durability over 20 years
item.description: Saudi Arabia’s Roads General Authority (RGA) is utilizing an advanced Heavy Vehicle Simulator (HVS) to evaluate road durability over a simulated 20-year lifespan. This cutting-edge technology, the first of its kind in the Gulf region, tests road performance under various traffic, climate, and geological conditions, enhancing infrastructure project management and supporting the Kingdom's road safety and quality improvement goals.

item.title: Rescuers say 39 missing in Indonesia factory fire
item.description: JAKARTA: Indonesian rescue workers were searching for 39 missing people on Sunday after a confectionery factory caught fire west of Jakarta, a rescue official said. The Fonusa Agung Mulia factory, located in the Serang district around 50 kilometers (31 miles) from the capital, caught fire on Saturday afternoon, a local search and rescue agency said in a statement. item.title: US immigration officers make arrests at Seattle airport in ‘distressing’ scene, delaying flight
item.description: Immigration officers detained two individuals at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport during the boarding of an Alaska Airlines flight, causing distress among passengers and delaying the flight. The arrests were part of a targeted operation against those overstaying visas, leading to vocal protests from witnesses, including a family member who claimed to have a work permit. The incident has sparked criticism from local officials and raised concerns about ICE's enforcement tactics during a busy travel period.

item.title: The secret courage of Australia’s Bondi shooting hero, one year on
item.description: SYDNEY: A man who heroically tackled a gunman at a Jewish festival on Bondi Beach said his wounds still ache as he issued a plea for unity almost a year after Australia’s worst mass shooting in decades. Fruit seller Ahmed al Ahmed, who was born in Syria and moved to Australia in 2006, was visiting the Sydney beach with his cousin on a Sunday afternoon last December when he heard shots ring out. item.title: Little Mercury gets its first visitor in years as a pair of spacecraft loop into orbit
item.description: CAPE CANAVERAL, Florida: A pair of spacecraft slipped into orbit around Mercury on Saturday after an eight-year cruise through the inner solar system to unravel our littlest planet’s mountain of mysteries. The linked robotic explorers — one European, the other Japanese — will separate from one another next month in order to map and study the scorching little planet from different altitudes. item.title: Canada defense chief sees no change despite reported US military curbs
item.description: Despite a reported Pentagon directive introducing new restrictions on military cooperation, Canadian Defense Minister David McGuinty emphasized that there has been no change in the collaboration between Canada and the United States. He stated that both nations continue to work closely on various military operations and that their defense relationship remains strong, with ongoing commitments to joint security initiatives until specific details of the reported directives are clarified.

item.title: Belgium faces air traffic shutdown due to national strike Monday
item.description: BRUSSELS, Belgium: Almost all flights are set to be canceled in Belgium on Monday after the country’s air traffic controller said its staff will take part in a national strike against government austerity measures. Skeyes, the company responsible for air traffic control in the country, said Saturday it will be unable to provide regular services at Belgian airports and in the airspace between 7:00 am (0600 GMT) and 9:00 p.m. (2000 GMT) on November 23. “The anticipated staffing levels will not all

item.title: Democrats who swept into the Senate promised change. A leadership vote is testing them early
item.description: Democrats are facing an early test of their commitment to change as they choose their Senate leadership ahead of being sworn in. The 13 newly elected senators, including progressives supporting Chris Van Hollen, are navigating differing opinions on whether to back incumbent Chuck Schumer or the challenger, highlighting a rift between traditional party leadership and calls for a more aggressive legislative approach.

item.title: Libya loses $30.8 million as armed group blocks oil pipeline for over 20 days
item.description: Libya has suffered a loss of $30.8 million in oil revenue after an armed group blocked the Hamada oil pipeline for more than 20 days, halting the transport of over 302,000 barrels of crude oil. The National Oil Corporation reported a reduction in crude output by 14,418 barrels per day, emphasizing that such disruptions undermine the country’s economy and efforts to restore confidence in its energy sector.

item.title: French protesters rally for sixth weekend over living costs, public services
item.description: PARIS, France: Tens of thousands of people marched in cities in France on Saturday, on the sixth weekend in a row of protests to demand better public services and express anger over the rising cost of living and inequality. The protest movement, sparked in mid-September by high school students demanding better learning conditions, fueled a nationwide campaign against soaring prices, inadequate public services and police brutality that spread across Europe, even as turnout in France has dwindled.

item.description: MUNICH: FIFPRO said on Saturday it was “deeply concerned” by public comments from Bayern Munich’s leadership about Jamal Musiala’s contract, accusing the German champions of putting pressure on the midfielder while he recovers from health problems. The global players’ union was responding to recent remarks by senior Bayern officials, including honorary president Uli Hoeness, CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen and supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, about Musiala’s future at the club. item.title: Alcaraz to face Zverev for ATP Finals title
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz secured a spot in the ATP Finals title match by defeating Ben Shelton 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (7/1) and will face world number one Alexander Zverev, who triumphed over Daniil Medvedev. Despite battling a thigh injury, Alcaraz aims to avenge his loss in last year's final and capture his first ATP Finals title.

item.title: Nmecha helps Dortmund beat Gladbach to top Bundesliga
item.description: Felix Nmecha’s late goal gave Borussia Dortmund a 1-0 win over Borussia Moenchengladbach, putting them at the top of the Bundesliga.

item.title: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu’s party for Israeli coalition talks
item.description: Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the centrist Yashar party, has invited Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party for coalition discussions to form a new Israeli government. The talks are set to begin on Sunday with a focus on establishing a broad governance coalition.

item.title: 24 dead in Nigeria when boat capsizes while carrying people to a funeral
item.description: A boat carrying people to a funeral in Nigeria’s Bayelsa State capsized, resulting in at least 24 deaths. Search and rescue operations continue with some missing persons unaccounted for.

item.description: PSG’s Desire Doue suffered a severe knee injury during their Ligue 1 win against Nice, which ended 3-2. He was taken off the field on a stretcher shortly after scoring a goal.
